The passage explains that renewable energy technologies such as solar and wind power are promising, but their integration into existing power grids is difficult. The key issue highlighted is intermittency, which means the energy supply is irregular because it depends on weather conditions. When sunlight or wind is not available, energy production drops, and this creates instability in the power system. As a result, fossil-fuel backup or expensive storage methods are required. None of the other options—public support, government regulation, or transportation costs—are mentioned as central problems. Therefore, the primary challenge discussed in the passage is intermittency in energy supply.
